title: What Is a Verb?
sourceNote: The auto-captions are heavily garbled; the verb lists were reconstructed from context, so a few verbs may differ slightly from the video.
objectives: I can explain what a verb is
I can find the stem and the ending of an infinitive
I can explain why verbs are conjugated
I can tell regular and irregular verbs apart

grammar.title: What is a verb?
grammar.body: A **verb** describes an action or a state: *spielen* (to play), *lernen* (to learn). The verb is the core of the sentence, and the sentence structure depends on it.

grammar.title: Infinitive: stem and ending
grammar.body: The basic form of a verb is the **infinitive**. You find it in the dictionary. It always has two parts: the **stem** (*Verbstamm*) and the ending (*Endung*). Almost all German infinitives end in **-en**, a few in **-n**. The best way to learn a verb is to learn its infinitive.

grammar.title: Conjugation depends on the subject
grammar.body: In a sentence the verb must be **conjugated**: you keep the stem and add an ending that fits the subject. Two things decide the ending: the **person** (1st, 2nd, 3rd) and **singular or plural**. This is why you learned the personal pronouns in lesson 11. The same verb changes with the subject: *ich komme*, but *wir kommen*.

grammar.title: Regular and irregular verbs
grammar.body:
**Regular verbs** (*regelmäßige Verben*, also called weak verbs) keep their stem in every form. Example: *lernen* has the stem *lern* in *ich lerne, du lernst, wir lernen*.

**Irregular verbs** (*unregelmäßige Verben*, strong verbs) change their stem vowel in some forms, e.g. *sprechen*: *du sprichst*. The endings stay the same as for regular verbs. A few verbs keep the stem but are still irregular. You will conjugate regular verbs in lesson 14 and irregular verbs in lesson 15.

Examples
rows: sprechen, lesen, sehen, nehmen, treffen, fahren

mistakes.why: The verb must be conjugated; do not use the infinitive after *ich*.
*sprechen* is irregular: e becomes i with *du*.

tip: Always learn a new verb in its infinitive form and mark it R (regular) or I (irregular).

comprehension.a: The person and whether the subject is singular or plural.

comprehension.q: What is the difference between regular and irregular verbs?
comprehension.a: Regular verbs keep their stem; irregular verbs change the stem vowel in some forms.
